sentences.en: From NPR, this is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是 NPR，欢迎收听《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: It all started at a live fish and meat market in Wuhan, a city in central China.
sentences.zh: 这一切始于中国中部城市武汉的一家活鱼活肉市场。

sentences.en: No one knows exactly how or when, but one day late last year,
sentences.zh: 没人确切知道是怎么回事或发生在何时，但去年年底的一天，

sentences.en: a coronavirus leaped from an animal into a human.
sentences.zh: 一种冠状病毒从动物身上传染给了人类。

sentences.en: Before long, people all around Wuhan started getting sick.
sentences.zh: 没过多久，武汉各地的人们开始生病。

sentences.en: We know what happened next.
sentences.zh: 接下来的事我们都知道了。

sentences.en: To curb the spread of this coronavirus,
sentences.zh: 为了遏制这种冠状病毒的传播，

sentences.en: China announced a draconian lockdown of more than 11 million people in Wuhan.
sentences.zh: 中国宣布对武汉超过 1100 万人口实施严厉的封城措施。

sentences.en: No one in, no one out.
sentences.zh: 只许出，不许进。

sentences.en: What we're seeing and hearing on the internet is police in hazmat suits going door to door,
sentences.zh: 我们在网上看到和听到的是，身穿防护服的警察挨家挨户上门，

sentences.en: taking people away who either have a fever or are rumored to have been in contact with someone who did.
sentences.zh: 带走那些发烧的人，或者据传与感染者有过接触的人。

sentences.en: Containment is the goal here, and using whatever means is necessary.
sentences.zh: 这里的目标是控制疫情，为此不惜一切代价。

sentences.en: By the time China had set up these containment measures, the virus had slipped outside of Wuhan.
sentences.zh: 当中国采取这些防控措施时，病毒已经溜出了武汉。

sentences.en: It began spreading to other places across the globe, from South Korea...
sentences.zh: 它开始蔓延到全球其他地方，从韩国……

sentences.en: Two patients may have contracted the disease from someone who was infected here in the nation,
sentences.zh: 两名患者可能是在国内被感染者传染的，

sentences.en: or Hongyu is standing by on the line for us...
sentences.zh: 或者红宇正在线上为我们待命……

sentences.en: ...to Italy.
sentences.zh: ……到意大利。

sentences.en: ...stretta del governo con le misure di contenimento dell'epidemia per la regione Lombardia e quattordici province...
sentences.zh: ……政府对伦巴第大区和 14 个省份采取了严格的防疫措施……

sentences.en: ...se entra e si esce...
sentences.zh: ……禁止进出……

sentences.en: Northern Italy emerged as an early hotspot for that nation.
sentences.zh: 意大利北部成为了该国早期的疫情热点地区。

sentences.en: Near the end of February, the Italian government began imposing travel restrictions on residents of the Lombardy region.
sentences.zh: 二月底，意大利政府开始对伦巴第大区的居民实施旅行限制。

sentences.en: But it was too late.
sentences.zh: 但为时已晚。

sentences.en: On March 8th, with the virus spreading wildly, the government locked down some 16 million people in Lombardy and 14 neighboring provinces.
sentences.zh: 3 月 8 日，随着病毒疯狂蔓延，政府封锁了伦巴第及周边 14 个省份，涉及约 1600 万人口。

sentences.en: In theory, it means that people are not supposed to leave those areas,
sentences.zh: 理论上，这意味着人们不准离开这些地区，

sentences.en: but in fact the authorities simply haven't had the time and perhaps not even the resources to make this a reality.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，当局根本没有时间，甚至可能没有资源来落实这一点。

sentences.en: In Milan and in other areas affected by the lockdown, people race to train stations, trying to get out before it's too late.
sentences.zh: 在米兰和其他受封锁影响的地区，人们争先恐后地涌向火车站，试图在为时已晚之前离开。

sentences.en: Many of those people fleeing Lombardy brought the virus with them to other parts of Italy.
sentences.zh: 许多逃离伦巴第的人将病毒带到了意大利的其他地区。

sentences.en: Very soon, the death toll in Italy versus the death toll in China told its own story.
sentences.zh: 很快，意大利的死亡人数与中国的死亡人数对比，说明了一切。

sentences.en: It feels like a hole that Italy just can't plug.
sentences.zh: 感觉就像是一个意大利怎么也堵不住的漏洞。

sentences.en: The daily loss of hundreds of lives.
sentences.zh: 每天都有数百人丧生。

sentences.en: Coronavirus fatalities in this country of 60 million people, now higher than in China, with a population of one and a half billion.
sentences.zh: 在这个 6000 万人口的国家，冠状病毒的死亡人数现在超过了拥有 15 亿人口的中国。

sentences.en: It's brought one of the world's best healthcare systems to its knees.
sentences.zh: 这让世界上最好的医疗系统之一陷入了瘫痪。

sentences.en: The story of the coronavirus outbreak is still being written.
sentences.zh: 冠状病毒爆发的故事仍在书写之中。

sentences.en: We don't yet know all the lessons that will be drawn from the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 我们还不知道能从这场大流行中吸取哪些教训。

sentences.en: There are still details that have not been fully divulged, including whether the Chinese government has revealed the true scope of the outbreak.
sentences.zh: 仍有一些细节尚未完全披露，包括中国政府是否揭示了疫情的真实规模。

sentences.en: That said, are there early lessons we can draw from the outbreak and how nations have responded?
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，我们能从这次疫情以及各国如何应对中吸取什么早期教训吗？

sentences.en: This week on Hidden Brain, we're going to look at how nations and individuals think about rules,
sentences.zh: 本周在《隐藏的大脑》节目中，我们将探讨各国和个人是如何看待规则的，

sentences.en: both in moments of crisis and in everyday interactions.
sentences.zh: 无论是在危机时刻还是在日常互动中。

sentences.en: Cultural attitudes about rule-following and rule-breaking shape our lives in all kinds of ways,
sentences.zh: 关于遵守规则和破坏规则的文化态度，以各种方式塑造着我们的生活，

sentences.en: from the tidiness of our homes, to our political preferences, to our approach to stopping the spread of a pandemic.
sentences.zh: 从我们家里的整洁程度，到我们的政治偏好，再到我们应对大流行传播的方式。

sentences.en: Michelle Gelfand is a psychologist at the University of Maryland.
sentences.zh: 米歇尔·格尔凡德是马里兰大学的心理学家。

sentences.en: She studies how organizations, communities, and nations are shaped by their cultures.
sentences.zh: 她研究组织、社区和国家是如何被其文化所塑造的。

sentences.en: She's the author of the book Rulemakers, Rule Breakers.
sentences.zh: 她是《规则制定者，规则破坏者》一书的作者。

sentences.en: Where others might see only policy differences between nations and how they respond to a pandemic,
sentences.zh: 当别人可能只看到各国在应对大流行时的政策差异时，

sentences.en: Michelle Gelfand sees the hidden hand of culture.
sentences.zh: 米歇尔·格尔凡德看到了文化这只“隐形之手”。

sentences.en: It shapes choices, decisions, and outcomes.
sentences.zh: 它塑造了选择、决策和结果。

sentences.en: Michelle Gelfand, welcome to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 米歇尔·格尔凡德，欢迎来到《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: Great to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴来到这里。

sentences.en: A lot of your work involves paying attention to things that are familiar and seeing them with fresh eyes.
sentences.zh: 你的很多工作涉及关注那些熟悉的事物，并以全新的视角审视它们。

sentences.en: I want to look at a few of these examples.
sentences.zh: 我想看几个例子。

sentences.en: You talk early in the book about a pedestrian in Berlin standing at a traffic intersection at 11 o'clock in the night.
sentences.zh: 你在书的开头谈到一位柏林的行人，在深夜 11 点站在十字路口。

sentences.en: There isn't a car in sight.
sentences.zh: 视线范围内没有一辆车。

sentences.en: Does she cross the road?
sentences.zh: 她会过马路吗？

sentences.en: She crosses the road when the light turns green, but stays put even if there's no cars around.
sentences.zh: 她会在绿灯亮时过马路，但即使周围没有车，她也会原地等待。

sentences.en: And of course, a continent away in Boston, we don't see the same thing happening even though it's Russia and there might be a sign saying don't walk.
sentences.zh: 当然，在相隔一个大洲的波士顿，我们看不到同样的情况，即使那是红灯，而且可能还有写着“禁止通行”的标志。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: In Boston, New York, my hometown originally, you see jaywalkers incessantly crossing the street, even with kids in tow.
sentences.zh: 在波士顿、纽约——我最初的家乡，你会看到行人不停地乱穿马路，甚至带着孩子。

sentences.en: And of course, all of us have seen this.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们所有人都见过这种情况。

sentences.en: As we've gone to different cities and different countries, we sort of noticed that people behave differently.
sentences.zh: 当我们去过不同的城市和国家时，我们注意到人们的行为方式不同。

sentences.en: The interesting thing is that we don't actually stop to marvel at how consistent those differences are across places.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，我们实际上并没有停下来惊叹这些差异在不同地方是多么一致。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It's really a puzzle because culture is omnipresent.
sentences.zh: 这确实是一个谜，因为文化无处不在。

sentences.en: It's all around us, but it's invisible.
sentences.zh: 它就在我们周围，但它是隐形的。

sentences.en: We really take it for granted, even though it's shaping our behavior from morning until night.
sentences.zh: 我们真的把它视为理所当然，尽管它从早到晚都在塑造我们的行为。

sentences.en: And often it's only the case when you get outside of your culture that you realize you've been so profoundly shaped by your own socialization and norm-following or norm-breaking.
sentences.zh: 而且通常只有当你走出自己的文化时，你才会意识到自己被自身的社会化以及对规范的遵守或破坏塑造得如此深刻。

sentences.en: Yeah, there's the old joke about the fish in the water, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 是的，关于水里的鱼的那个老笑话，不是吗？

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Two fish are swimming around and then they pass by another fish who says to them, hey, boys, how's the water?
sentences.zh: 两条鱼在游来游去，然后它们经过另一条鱼，那条鱼对它们说：“嘿，伙计们，水怎么样？”

sentences.en: And they swim on and one turns to the other and says, what the heck is water?
sentences.zh: 它们继续游，其中一条转向另一条说：“水到底是什么鬼东西？”

sentences.en: And it's really funny because this illustrates a profound point, which is that sometimes it's the most important realities around us that we don't really see.
sentences.zh: 这真的很有趣，因为它说明了一个深刻的道理，那就是有时我们周围最重要的现实，我们反而看不见。

sentences.en: And for fish, that's water.
sentences.zh: 对于鱼来说，那是水。

sentences.en: But for humans, that's culture.
sentences.zh: 但对于人类来说，那是文化。

sentences.en: So you have lots of examples in the book that talk about this.
sentences.zh: 所以你在书里有很多例子谈到了这一点。

sentences.en: I understand the Swiss bank UBS has a dress code that's actually written down?
sentences.zh: 我听说瑞士银行瑞银集团有一份书面的着装规范？

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It had been for many years, like 30 some odd pages of dress codes.
sentences.zh: 多年来一直如此，大概有 30 多页的着装规范。

sentences.en: And you can see that the strictness of rules is found in so many different places.
sentences.zh: 你可以看到，规则的严格程度在许多不同的地方都有体现。

sentences.en: In Singapore, for example, you're not allowed to bring in large quantities of gum.
sentences.zh: 例如在新加坡，你不允许携带大量口香糖。

sentences.en: And for people who do that, they can get fined pretty seriously, including things like littering or spitting on the street.
sentences.zh: 对于这样做的人，他们可能会受到相当严重的罚款，包括乱扔垃圾或在街上吐痰等行为。

sentences.en: These things can be strictly punished in Singapore.
sentences.zh: 这些事情在新加坡会受到严厉惩罚。

sentences.en: In fact, even if you're walking around your house naked in front of the curtains with them open, this can get you a hefty fine in Singapore.
sentences.zh: 事实上，即使你在家里赤身裸体地在窗帘前走动，如果窗帘没拉上，在新加坡也可能让你面临巨额罚款。

sentences.en: It's called the fine nation because it's known for having a lot of punishments for seemingly minor offenses.
sentences.zh: 它被称为“罚款之国”，因为它以对看似轻微的违规行为进行大量惩罚而闻名。

sentences.en: I'm guessing that these rules wouldn't go down so well in Sao Paulo.
sentences.zh: 我猜这些规则在圣保罗可能行不通。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: We could see that there's much more permissiveness in places like Brazil and New Zealand and the United States, to some extent, where you find a slew of norm violations every day,
sentences.zh: 我们可以看到，在巴西、新西兰和美国等地方，宽容度要高得多，在那里你每天都能发现大量的违规行为，

sentences.en: whether it's people walking barefoot in banks in New Zealand and decorating their fences with thousands of bras and burning couches on university campuses or showing up to work really super late.
sentences.zh: 无论是人们在新西兰赤脚走进银行，还是用成千上万件胸罩装饰栅栏，在大学校园里烧沙发，或者上班严重迟到。

sentences.en: It's astonishing, the sort of differences around the world in terms of people who are making the rules or breaking them.
sentences.zh: 世界各地在制定规则或破坏规则方面存在这种差异，真是令人惊讶。

sentences.en: I love the example you give in the book that Brazilians actually have a phrase for when they plan to be on time for a meeting.
sentences.zh: 我很喜欢你在书中举的例子，巴西人甚至有一个短语来形容他们计划准时参加会议的时候。

sentences.en: They call it compontualidade britannica.
sentences.zh: 他们称之为“英国式准时”。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's really follow the rules like they do in Britain.
sentences.zh: 那真的是像英国人那样遵守规则。

sentences.en: When they want to make sure that people are on time, they have to remind themselves that they have their own culture,
sentences.zh: 当他们想确保人们准时时，他们必须提醒自己，他们有自己的文化，

sentences.en: their own norms of basically not really having a whole lot of rules around time.
sentences.zh: 他们自己的规范基本上就是对时间没有太多的规则。

sentences.en: So when you're working, obviously, across cultures,
sentences.zh: 所以当你显然在跨文化工作时，

sentences.en: you can see this would be pretty frustrating where people have differences in their rules around basic things like time and how organized they are, how synchronized they are,
sentences.zh: 你会发现这相当令人沮丧，因为人们在时间等基本事情上的规则存在差异，以及他们的组织程度、同步程度，

sentences.en: how much punishment they give for even seemingly minor things.
sentences.zh: 以及他们对看似轻微的事情给予多少惩罚。

sentences.en: You know,
sentences.zh: 你知道，

sentences.en: I remember visiting Rio de Janeiro many years ago and I attended a soccer match at Maracana Stadium and there were these plastic seats that we were all sitting on and at one point the fan sitting next to me was very upset with the player who had made a mistake and so he got up and started screaming at this player and he called him,
sentences.zh: 我记得多年前访问里约热内卢时，我参加了马拉卡纳体育场的一场足球比赛，我们都坐在塑料座椅上，当时坐在我旁边的球迷对一个犯错的球员非常不满，于是他站起来开始对着那个球员尖叫，他称他为——

sentences.en: how shall I put this, he called the player the illegitimate child of a sex worker.
sentences.zh: 我该怎么说呢，他称那个球员是性工作者的私生子。

sentences.en: Let me just put it that way.
sentences.zh: 我就这么说吧。

sentences.en: And then he kicked the plastic seat in front of him so that it flew over the heads of the fans in the next three rows.
sentences.zh: 然后他踢了前面的塑料座椅，座椅飞过了后面三排球迷的头顶。

sentences.en: And what was amazing to me was not just that he did this, but that absolutely no one paid him any attention.
sentences.zh: 让我惊讶的不仅是他做了这件事，而是绝对没有人理会他。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's interesting.
sentences.zh: 是的，这很有趣。

sentences.en: There's stories of people who are visiting Brazil, including Japanese players and fans during the World Cup that had very different types of behaviors.
sentences.zh: 有关于访问巴西的人的故事，包括世界杯期间的日本球员和球迷，他们的行为方式非常不同。

sentences.en: If you're from Japan or Senegal, apparently you do your part to clean up your mess.
sentences.zh: 如果你来自日本或塞内加尔，显然你会尽自己的一份力量清理垃圾。

sentences.en: What?
sentences.zh: 什么？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: After the World Cup,
sentences.zh: 世界杯结束后，

sentences.en: the Japanese were cleaning up the stadium and it was astonishing to people to see this kind of organized action among Japanese in these Brazilian contexts where you see a whole host of disorderly behavior that people don't even notice because it's so typical.
sentences.zh: 日本人清理了体育场，人们看到日本人在这种巴西背景下表现出这种有组织的行动，感到非常惊讶，因为在那里你看到的是各种各样的混乱行为，人们甚至都没有注意到，因为这太典型了。

sentences.en: We are so familiar with these differences between groups that we have movies and television shows that are built around these themes.
sentences.zh: 我们对群体之间的这些差异非常熟悉，以至于我们有围绕这些主题制作的电影和电视节目。

sentences.en: These differences also show up in our domestic lives and in workplaces.
sentences.zh: 这些差异也出现在我们的家庭生活和工作场所中。

sentences.en: You can think about how strict or permissive we are from many different perspectives, from national perspective, from organizations and even our own households.
sentences.zh: 你可以从许多不同的角度思考我们的严格或宽容程度，从国家角度、组织角度，甚至是我们自己的家庭。

sentences.en: In the book, I talk about how we all have our own preference for the kind of Muppet we want to be.
sentences.zh: 在书中，我谈到了我们每个人都有自己想成为哪种布偶的偏好。

sentences.en: Some people are order Muppets.
sentences.zh: 有些人是“秩序布偶”。

sentences.en: Hello, this is Kermit the Frog.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是青蛙科米特。

sentences.en: And I am here today to offer to you the frog.
sentences.zh: 我今天在这里是来为你提供青蛙的。

sentences.en: They really like rules.
sentences.zh: 他们真的很喜欢规则。

sentences.en: They manage their impulses and they really like a lot of order and structure.
sentences.zh: 他们管理自己的冲动，他们非常喜欢秩序和结构。

sentences.en: And then on the flip side, some people are chaos Muppets.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，有些人是“混乱布偶”。

sentences.en: Hello.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: Think Cookie Monster.
sentences.zh: 想想饼干怪兽。

sentences.en: They tend to not really notice rules.
sentences.zh: 他们往往不太注意规则。

sentences.en: They are more risk-taking and impulsive and they're more tolerant of ambiguity.
sentences.zh: 他们更喜欢冒险和冲动，对模糊性的容忍度更高。

sentences.en: No, cookies, cookies.
sentences.zh: 不，饼干，饼干。

sentences.en: It causes a lot of conflict between people.
sentences.zh: 这在人与人之间引起了很多冲突。

sentences.en: Think about parents who are trying to raise kids and they have different ideas in terms of how strict they should be or finances or even how you load the dishwasher I found in my household can get you a little flack.
sentences.zh: 想想那些试图抚养孩子的父母，他们在应该有多严格、财务问题，甚至是我发现的在我家里如何装洗碗机等方面有不同的想法，这可能会让你受到一点指责。

sentences.en: So I think it's important to really look at this as an aspect of culture that affects us all the time from our nations to our households.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，真正将其视为一种影响我们所有人的文化层面是很重要的，从我们的国家到我们的家庭。

sentences.en: I have to ask you about the dishwasher.
sentences.zh: 我必须问你关于洗碗机的事。

sentences.en: What's the conflict in your household?
sentences.zh: 你们家里的冲突是什么？

sentences.en: Well, I tend to lean looser.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我倾向于更宽松。

sentences.en: My husband, who's a lawyer, leans tighter for good reasons.
sentences.zh: 我丈夫是一名律师，出于正当理由，他倾向于更严格。

sentences.en: He's an occupation where there's a lot of accountability, a lot of standards and monitoring.
sentences.zh: 他的职业有很多问责制、很多标准和监督。

sentences.en: And I tend to be a little bit on the looser side.
sentences.zh: 而我倾向于稍微宽松一点。

sentences.en: And so he finds it really unbelievably disturbing when I load the dishwasher because I don't really pay attention to how organized it is.
sentences.zh: 所以当我装洗碗机时，他觉得这真的令人难以置信地不安，因为我并不真正注意它有多整洁。

sentences.en: Or if I leave towels on the bed, I get a little bit of feedback.
sentences.zh: 或者如果我把毛巾留在床上，我会得到一点反馈。

sentences.en: We've come to really try to negotiate these differences by trying to think about what domains do we need to be tight in and what domains can we be looser in.
sentences.zh: 我们已经真正尝试通过思考我们需要在哪些领域保持严格，在哪些领域可以更宽松来协商这些差异。

sentences.en: And we even talk about it with the kids and we try to think about what's our priorities.
sentences.zh: 我们甚至和孩子们谈论它，我们试着思考我们的优先事项是什么。

sentences.en: You know, what's really important to each of us as we try to organize on the strength of rules in the house.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当我们试图在家里组织规则的力量时，对我们每个人来说真正重要的是什么。

sentences.en: Because as you point out,
sentences.zh: 因为正如你指出的，

sentences.en: there might be domains where actually it's perfectly fine to have fairly lackadaisical rules and other domains where it's actually catastrophic to have lackadaisical rules.
sentences.zh: 可能有些领域确实可以有相当随意的规则，而其他领域如果规则太随意则是灾难性的。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's exactly the point.
sentences.zh: 是的，这正是重点。

sentences.en: So in our house, just to give you a sense of the negotiation and how it played out,
sentences.zh: 所以为了让你了解我们的协商以及它是如何进行的，

sentences.en: we finally did agree that some domains like our health and how much we work in terms of studying hard for the kids for school are really important to be strict about.
sentences.zh: 我们最终确实同意，一些领域，比如我们的健康，以及孩子们在学校努力学习方面，严格要求是非常重要的。

sentences.en: But other things like your bedtime or how messy you are, that was a tough negotiation because the house is kind of a mess and drives Todd crazy.
sentences.zh: 但其他事情，比如你的就寝时间或者你有多乱，那是一场艰难的谈判，因为家里有点乱，这让托德快疯了。

sentences.en: But those are domains that could be much looser.
sentences.zh: 但这些领域可以宽松得多。

sentences.en: We have to give some domains where people can have freedom to just do what they want, but we need to know which are the priority domains to be more strict in.
sentences.zh: 我们必须提供一些领域，让人们有自由去做他们想做的事，但我们需要知道哪些是优先领域，以便在这些领域更加严格。

sentences.en: Especially in a country like the United States, which is built around the idea of freedom, rules can seem onerous.
sentences.zh: 特别是在像美国这样一个建立在自由理念之上的国家，规则可能会显得繁琐。

sentences.en: Why can't we just pick and choose the rules that work best for us?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们不能只挑选最适合我们的规则呢？

sentences.en: Michelle says we might not like rules, but we would probably like a country with no rules, even less.
sentences.zh: 米歇尔说，我们可能不喜欢规则，但我们可能更不喜欢一个没有规则的国家。

sentences.en: Imagine a world without any kind of rules.
sentences.zh: 想象一个没有任何规则的世界。

sentences.en: Just do a thought experiment where you go outside and people are driving on whatever side of the road they feel like and they're ignoring traffic lights.
sentences.zh: 做一个思想实验，你走到外面，人们随意在道路的任何一侧开车，并且无视交通信号灯。

sentences.en: Or think about going to your favorite restaurant and people are chewing with their mouths wide open and they're stealing food off people's plates.
sentences.zh: 或者想想去你最喜欢的餐馆，人们张着大嘴咀嚼，还从别人的盘子里偷食物。

sentences.en: That sounds like my New York family, actually.
sentences.zh: 说实话，这听起来像我纽约的家人。

sentences.en: Or imagine that you board a crowded elevator and you find people facing backwards and shaking their umbrellas all over the place.
sentences.zh: 或者想象你走进一部拥挤的电梯，发现人们背对着站立，还到处甩雨伞。

sentences.en: I encourage the listeners to see what happens if you do something like that.
sentences.zh: 我鼓励听众去看看如果你那样做会发生什么。

sentences.en: What kind of responses do you get?
sentences.zh: 你会得到什么样的反应？

sentences.en: Or imagine a world where people are having sex all over the place on buses, airplanes, in movie theaters.
sentences.zh: 或者想象一个人们在公共汽车、飞机、电影院里到处发生性行为的世界。

sentences.en: This is a world without social norms or any agreed-upon standards for behavior.
sentences.zh: 这是一个没有社会规范或任何公认行为标准的社会。

sentences.en: And luckily, we have invented these kinds of rules to avoid these scenarios.
sentences.zh: 幸运的是，我们发明了这些规则来避免这些情况。

sentences.en: In a way, you can think about it as societies would cease to function without these kinds of rules.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，你可以认为如果没有这些规则，社会将无法运转。

sentences.en: They're the glue that binds us together.
sentences.zh: 它们是将我们凝聚在一起的粘合剂。

sentences.en: What Michelle is talking about is not just the rules we have, but the rules we have about following the rules.
sentences.zh: 米歇尔所说的不仅仅是我们拥有的规则，而是我们关于遵守规则的规则。

sentences.en: Are we exacting about our preferences for order and structure?
sentences.zh: 我们对秩序和结构的偏好是否严苛？

sentences.en: Or do we prefer to have wiggle room?
sentences.zh: 还是我们更喜欢有回旋余地？

sentences.en: When we come back, we dig into Michelle's framework for understanding these preferences.
sentences.zh: 回来后，我们将深入探讨米歇尔理解这些偏好的框架。

sentences.en: What does it take to really make amends?
sentences.zh: 真正做出补偿需要什么？

sentences.en: And how should we navigate our digital spaces?
sentences.zh: 我们应该如何驾驭我们的数字空间？

sentences.en: I'm Anoush Samarodi.
sentences.zh: 我是阿努什·萨马罗迪。

sentences.en: Each week on NPR's TED Radio Hour, we go on a journey with TED speakers who help us answer some of life's biggest questions.
sentences.zh: 每周在 NPR 的 TED 广播节目中，我们都会与 TED 演讲者一起踏上旅程，他们帮助我们回答生活中一些最大的问题。

sentences.en: Join us.
sentences.zh: 加入我们。

sentences.en: Listen now.
sentences.zh: 现在收听。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: I'm speaking with cross-cultural psychologist Michelle Gelfand at the University of Maryland.
sentences.zh: 我正在与马里兰大学的跨文化心理学家米歇尔·格尔凡德交谈。

sentences.en: Michelle, you talk at some length in the book about countries like Japan or New Zealand
sentences.zh: 米歇尔，你在书中详细谈到了像日本或新西兰这样的国家，

sentences.en: that are very different in terms of how much they care about following the rules.
sentences.zh: 它们在多大程度上关心遵守规则方面非常不同。

sentences.en: You also suggest in some ways that the history of these countries plays some role in how people come to think about the rules.
sentences.zh: 你还在某种程度上暗示，这些国家的历史在人们如何看待规则方面发挥了一定作用。

sentences.en: What do you mean by that?
sentences.zh: 你这话是什么意思？

sentences.en: Yeah, you know, I think that it's important to recognize that culture evolves for good reasons.
sentences.zh: 是的，你知道，我认为重要的是要认识到文化的发展是有充分理由的。

sentences.en: And if you look at places like Japan, you can see that they've been faced with chronic threat in their histories.
sentences.zh: 如果你看看像日本这样的地方，你可以看到它们在历史上一直面临着长期的威胁。

sentences.en: I mean, think about Mother Nature's fury, the constant natural disasters and famine that has been faced by the Japanese for centuries.
sentences.zh: 我是说，想想大自然的愤怒，几个世纪以来日本人一直面临的持续自然灾害和饥荒。

sentences.en: Or how many times they've been potentially involved in conflict on their own soil.
sentences.zh: 或者他们有多少次可能卷入自己领土上的冲突。

sentences.en: Contrast that with New Zealand, where there's been very little history of these kinds of threats on New Zealand's territory.
sentences.zh: 对比一下新西兰，那里在新西兰领土上几乎没有这种威胁的历史。

sentences.en: So it may not be that surprising that they develop very different mindsets over the course of their histories.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们在历史进程中发展出截然不同的思维方式也就不足为奇了。

sentences.en: And we need to understand those ecological and historical factors to really make sense of cultural differences.
sentences.zh: 我们需要理解那些生态和历史因素，才能真正理解文化差异。

sentences.en: So you would call a country like Japan culturally tight and a country like New Zealand culturally loose.
sentences.zh: 所以你会称像日本这样的国家为文化紧密型，而像新西兰这样的国家为文化松散型。

sentences.en: What do you mean by those terms, Michelle?
sentences.zh: 米歇尔，这些术语是什么意思？

sentences.en: So I mentioned earlier that all groups have social norms, these agreed upon standards of behavior.
sentences.zh: 我之前提到过，所有群体都有社会规范，即这些公认的行为标准。

sentences.en: And we needed these norms to basically coordinate and predict each other's behaviors.
sentences.zh: 我们需要这些规范来基本协调和预测彼此的行为。

sentences.en: They're the glue that binds us together.
sentences.zh: 它们是将我们凝聚在一起的粘合剂。

sentences.en: But what I've discovered is that that glue is stronger in some context than others.
sentences.zh: 但我发现，这种粘合剂在某些环境中比其他环境中更强。

sentences.en: Some cultures are tight, by which I mean that they have strict norms and punishments for people that are deviating from those norMs.
sentences.zh: 有些文化是紧密的，我的意思是，它们对偏离这些规范的人有严格的规范和惩罚。

sentences.en: And other groups are loose.
sentences.zh: 而其他群体则是松散的。

sentences.en: They have weaker norms and they're much more permissive.
sentences.zh: 它们的规范较弱，而且更加宽容。

sentences.en: And it's something that we can think about, this terminology, tight and loose, that can help us understand nations and states and organizations and even our own households.
sentences.zh: 我们可以思考这种术语，紧密和松散，这可以帮助我们理解国家、州、组织，甚至我们自己的家庭。

sentences.en: And so tightness and looseness is not about whether you have rules, but it's really about how much you follow the rules, how much you care about the rules,
sentences.zh: 所以紧密和松散并不是关于你是否有规则，而是关于你遵守规则的程度，你对规则的关心程度，

sentences.en: how important the rules are to you?
sentences.zh: 规则对你有多重要？

sentences.en: Tight cultures have a lot of rules and they're very strict about the enforcement of those rules.
sentences.zh: 紧密型文化有很多规则，而且对这些规则的执行非常严格。

sentences.en: Loose cultures have fewer rules that are actually much more ambiguous and they're much more permissive.
sentences.zh: 松散型文化规则较少，实际上更模糊，而且更加宽容。

sentences.en: They afford a wider range of behavior as permissible.
sentences.zh: 它们允许更广泛的行为。

sentences.en: Even in the same situation, think about a library, which many of us, as soon as we get into libraries, we know this is a tight situation.
sentences.zh: 即使在相同的情况下，想想图书馆，我们许多人一进入图书馆就知道这是一个紧密的情况。

sentences.en: You're not going to start singing and dancing and start playing your radio really loudly.
sentences.zh: 你不会开始唱歌跳舞，也不会大声播放收音机。

sentences.en: And around the world, libraries are pretty strict everywhere.
sentences.zh: 在世界各地，图书馆到处都很严格。

sentences.en: But what's remarkable, and this is what we can see in research, is that even in loose context,
sentences.zh: 但令人瞩目的是，这也是我们在研究中可以看到的，即使在松散的环境中，

sentences.en: people are doing all sorts of weird things in libraries compared to in tight cultures in the same situation.
sentences.zh: 与紧密文化中相同情况下的行为相比，人们在图书馆里做着各种奇怪的事情。

sentences.en: Or take a city park where it's much looser.
sentences.zh: 或者以城市公园为例，那里要松散得多。

sentences.en: There's a wider range of behavior that's permissible.
sentences.zh: 允许的行为范围更广。

sentences.en: We can see that in places like Pakistan.
sentences.zh: 我们可以在像巴基斯坦这样的地方看到这一点。

sentences.en: Yeah, there's much more behavior that's permissible in this context, but it's still stricter in public parks than in the United States.
sentences.zh: 是的，在这种情况下允许的行为要多得多，但公共公园仍然比美国更严格。

sentences.en: So we all have a normative radar thinking about which situations are tight and loose.
sentences.zh: 所以我们都有一个规范雷达，思考哪些情况是紧密的，哪些是松散的。

sentences.en: And we amazingly go through our days without even realizing it, that we're shifting our normative mindsets in these contexts.
sentences.zh: 令人惊讶的是，我们每天都在不知不觉中度过，我们在这些环境中转换我们的规范思维。

sentences.en: But nevertheless, we see wide variation in how people act in the same exact situations, libraries, public parks, elevators even, around the world.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，我们看到世界各地的人们在完全相同的情况下，如图书馆、公园、甚至电梯里的行为存在巨大差异。

sentences.en: So if you look at a country like Japan for a second, Michelle,
sentences.zh: 所以，米歇尔，如果你看一下像日本这样的国家，

sentences.en: you argue in the book that one of the drivers of the evolution of these tight cultures has to do with the experience of threat and historical threat.
sentences.zh: 你在书中指出，这些紧密文化演变的驱动力之一与威胁和历史威胁的经历有关。

sentences.en: Talk about that in the context of Japan.
sentences.zh: 谈谈日本背景下的这一点。

sentences.en: Yeah, so in this study that we did on tightness and looseness that was published in Science some years ago,
sentences.zh: 是的，在我们几年前发表在《科学》杂志上的关于紧密和松散的研究中，

sentences.en: we set out to study can we measure tightness and looseness around the world, recognizing that all cultures have tight and loose elements.
sentences.zh: 我们着手研究是否可以衡量世界各地的紧密和松散，认识到所有文化都有紧密和松散的元素。

sentences.en: We wanted to see can we classify countries like Japan and New Zealand and Greece and the Netherlands on a continuum of tightness and looseness.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看是否可以在紧密和松散的连续体上对日本、新西兰、希腊和荷兰等国家进行分类。

sentences.en: And that's what we did.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们所做的。

sentences.en: We can see that we can measure this construct and then we can say, well, why are these, what's explaining this variation?
sentences.zh: 我们可以看到我们可以衡量这个结构，然后我们可以说，好吧，为什么是这些，是什么解释了这种变化？

sentences.en: And I had a hunch that it might be related to the degree to which people need to coordinate their social action in the face of threat.
sentences.zh: 我有一种预感，这可能与人们在面对威胁时需要协调其社会行动的程度有关。

sentences.en: Now, not all tight cultures have threat, not all loose cultures lack it, but there seemed to be in our research a pretty significant connection between threats and tightness.
sentences.zh: 现在，并非所有紧密文化都有威胁，并非所有松散文化都缺乏威胁，但在我们的研究中，威胁和紧密之间似乎存在相当显著的联系。

sentences.en: So as I was collecting data around the world for this study, I was gathering data on the ecologies and the histories of these nations.
sentences.zh: 所以当我在世界各地为这项研究收集数据时，我正在收集关于这些国家的生态和历史的数据。

sentences.en: I got data on population density, for example, as far back as 1500.
sentences.zh: 例如，我获得了早在1500年的人口密度数据。

sentences.en: And I studied how many times a nation was potentially invaded on their own soil, not how much conflict they've been involved in around the world.
sentences.zh: 我研究了一个国家在自己的领土上可能被入侵的次数，而不是他们卷入世界各地冲突的次数。

sentences.en: The U.S., for example, has been involved in a lot of conflict.
sentences.zh: 例如，美国卷入了许多冲突。

sentences.en: But with some exceptions, we haven't had chronic invasions from Mexico and Canada, for example, across our history.
sentences.zh: 但除了一些例外，在我们的历史上，我们没有受到来自墨西哥和加拿大的长期入侵。

sentences.en: And what we were able to show in this study is that the countries that had a lot of threat tend to be tighter, like Japan and Germany and Austria,
sentences.zh: 我们在研究中能够证明的是，那些面临巨大威胁的国家往往更紧密，比如日本、德国和奥地利，

sentences.en: as compared to countries like New Zealand and Greece and Brazil that tend to have less threat.
sentences.zh: 与新西兰、希腊和巴西等往往威胁较小的国家相比。

sentences.en: And at a certain level, that makes perfect sense, isn't it, that if you've been through a lot of tough times,
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，这完全说得通，不是吗，如果你经历了很多艰难时期，

sentences.en: you sort of learned in some ways over time that it's important to hang together.
sentences.zh: 你随着时间的推移在某种程度上学会了团结一致是很重要的。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, it makes a lot of sense.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这很有道理。

sentences.en: When you have collective threat, you can't solve this on your own.
sentences.zh: 当你面临集体威胁时，你无法独自解决这个问题。

sentences.en: You need to really rely on other people in these situations to not defect, to not be egocentric, to coordinate at a scale to deal with the threat for survival.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，你真的需要依靠其他人不背叛，不以自我为中心，在一定规模上进行协调，以应对生存威胁。

sentences.en: And actually, we've seen in some of our computational models the same exact logic.
sentences.zh: 实际上，我们在一些计算模型中也看到了完全相同的逻辑。

sentences.en: As threat increases in our mathematical models, we see that groups tend to evolve to be tighter.
sentences.zh: 随着我们数学模型中威胁的增加，我们看到群体往往会演变得更加紧密。

sentences.en: So there seems to be something that may make evolutionary sense, that under a lot of threat, that we tend to tighten up.
sentences.zh: 所以似乎有一些东西可能具有进化意义，即在巨大的威胁下，我们往往会变得紧密。

sentences.en: You once ran a study at the University of Maryland where you manipulated people's attitudes or sense of threat by giving them a sense of overcrowding or a lack of overcrowding.
sentences.zh: 你曾经在马里兰大学进行过一项研究，通过给人们一种过度拥挤或不拥挤的感觉来操纵人们的态度或威胁感。

sentences.en: Tell me about that experiment and what you found, Misha.
sentences.zh: 告诉我那个实验以及你的发现，米莎。

sentences.en: Yeah, so we basically had two conditions in this experiment.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们在实验中基本上有两个条件。

sentences.en: In one condition, people were told that the University of Maryland had the highest or of the highest population density of campuses in the United States.
sentences.zh: 在一个条件下，人们被告知马里兰大学的人口密度是美国校园中最高的或最高的之一。

sentences.en: We showed them charts that showed this accompanying with quotes about how hard it was to find a seat in classrooms and to get lunch at the Union.
sentences.zh: 我们向他们展示了图表，并附上了关于在教室里找座位和在工会吃午餐有多难的引语。

sentences.en: And in another condition, we said the exact opposite.
sentences.zh: 在另一个条件下，我们说了完全相反的话。

sentences.en: We showed them pictures that showed that Maryland was very low population density, and it was really sometimes hard to even see people around.
sentences.zh: 我们向他们展示了图片，显示马里兰州的人口密度非常低，有时甚至很难看到周围有人。

sentences.en: But what we found was striking.
sentences.zh: 但我们的发现令人震惊。

sentences.en: In the high population density condition, when we asked people how bothered they were by norm violations,
sentences.zh: 在高人口密度条件下，当我们询问人们对规范违规行为感到多么困扰时，

sentences.en: we found that they were much more upset when people were violating norms as compared to the low population density condition.
sentences.zh: 我们发现与低人口密度条件相比，当人们违反规范时，他们会感到更加不安。

sentences.en: That suggests that we as humans can quickly tighten up in contexts where we think it makes sense.
sentences.zh: 这表明我们人类可以在我们认为有意义的环境中迅速变得紧密。

sentences.en: And we could see that in other studies where we prime terrorism threats or natural disaster threats.
sentences.zh: 我们可以在其他研究中看到这一点，我们在这些研究中启动了恐怖主义威胁或自然灾害威胁。

sentences.en: And we even see this in neuroscience studies.
sentences.zh: 我们甚至在神经科学研究中看到了这一点。

sentences.en: If threat is a driver of cultural tightness, Michelle finds that ethnic diversity is often a driver of cultural looseness.
sentences.zh: 如果威胁是文化紧密性的驱动力，米歇尔发现种族多样性往往是文化松散性的驱动力。

sentences.en: When people from different backgrounds come together, they have to find ways to adapt to one another.
sentences.zh: 当来自不同背景的人们聚在一起时，他们必须找到适应彼此的方法。

sentences.en: And that's tough to do if you're very rigid about the rules.
sentences.zh: 如果你对规则非常死板，那就很难做到。

sentences.en: Michelle conducted a survey of some 7,000 people from more than 30 countries.
sentences.zh: 米歇尔对来自30多个国家的约7000人进行了调查。

sentences.en: I asked her what she found about which countries were rule followers and which ones were rule breakers.
sentences.zh: 我问她关于哪些国家是规则遵守者，哪些是规则破坏者的发现。

sentences.en: In this study, we found that tight-loose was a continuum.
sentences.zh: 在这项研究中，我们发现紧密-松散是一个连续体。

sentences.en: Countries like Japan, Singapore, Germany, and Austria tended to veer tight.
sentences.zh: 像日本、新加坡、德国和奥地利这样的国家往往偏向紧密。

sentences.en: And countries like New Zealand, Brazil, the Netherlands, and Greece tended to veer loose.
sentences.zh: 而像新西兰、巴西、荷兰和希腊这样的国家往往偏向松散。

sentences.en: And of course, all countries have tight and loose elements.
sentences.zh: 当然，所有国家都有紧密和松散的元素。

sentences.en: In Japan, for example, even though it's pretty strict, there's designated times to kind of have fun and get drunk with your supervisors.
sentences.zh: 例如，在日本，尽管它相当严格，但也有指定的时间来娱乐和与主管喝酒。

sentences.en: And, you know, even in other contexts like New Zealand, which veers loose in our data, where you see people walking barefoot in banks around the country, for example.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，即使在像新西兰这样的其他环境中，我们的数据中它偏向松散，例如，你看到人们在全国各地的银行里赤脚行走。

sentences.en: There's also domains that are pretty tight in New Zealand that manifests itself when people are trying to stand out.
sentences.zh: 新西兰也有一些相当紧密的领域，当人们试图脱颖而出时，这一点就会显现出来。

sentences.en: They call them tall poppies.
sentences.zh: 他们称之为高罂粟。

sentences.en: New Zealand's a place that's high on egalitarianism.
sentences.zh: 新西兰是一个高度平等主义的地方。

sentences.en: So standing out is really violating that strong value.
sentences.zh: 所以脱颖而出真的违反了那个强烈的价值观。

sentences.en: And that's why that's a domain that's pretty tight in New Zealand.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么那个领域在新西兰相当紧密。

sentences.en: My theory would be that any domain that's really super important in a country evolves to be tight.
sentences.zh: 我的理论是，任何在一个国家非常重要的领域都会演变成紧密。

sentences.en: And so in New Zealand, we can see that when you break the rules of being egalitarian, you can get some serious negative feedback, whereas in many other domains, it's pretty loose.
sentences.zh: 所以，在新西兰，我们可以看到，当你打破平等主义的规则时，你可能会得到一些严重的负面反馈，而在许多其他领域，它相当松散。

sentences.en: So I'm wondering if what you said just now actually explains why if you look at countries like Pakistan or India, which were among the tightest nations in your sample,
sentences.zh: 所以我很好奇，你刚才说的是否实际上解释了为什么如果你看看像巴基斯坦或印度这样的国家，它们是你样本中最紧密的国家之一，

sentences.en: you can also see a significant amount of rule breaking.
sentences.zh: 你也可以看到大量的规则破坏。

sentences.en: So, you know, if anyone's driven a car in India or Pakistan, they would not say that these are countries that are hell-bent on following the rules.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，如果有人在印度或巴基斯坦开过车，他们不会说这些国家是执意要遵守规则的。

sentences.en: Yeah, well, I think that that's a really great example of that.
sentences.zh: 是的，好吧，我认为这是一个非常好的例子。

sentences.en: There can be domains that every country has that are tight or loose.
sentences.zh: 每个国家都可能存在紧密或松散的领域。

sentences.en: In Pakistan and India, you see that kind of public behavior of driving.
sentences.zh: 在巴基斯坦和印度，你可以看到那种驾驶的公共行为。

sentences.en: Egypt is another example.
sentences.zh: 埃及是另一个例子。

sentences.en: I've spent a lot of time in Egypt, and I just close my eyes when I'm in a taxi and just hope for the beSt.
sentences.zh: 我在埃及待了很长时间，当我在出租车里时，我只是闭上眼睛，祈祷一切顺利。

sentences.en: But in other domains, in terms of like gender and authority and religion, they evolve to be very tight.
sentences.zh: 但在其他领域，就性别、权威和宗教而言，它们演变得非常紧密。

sentences.en: So it's really important to kind of take that microscope and then zoom in and try to understand in any country, in any context, what domains are tight and what domains are loose.
sentences.zh: 所以，重要的是要用显微镜观察，然后放大，试图理解在任何国家、任何环境中，哪些领域是紧密的，哪些领域是松散的。

sentences.en: Michelle has also analyzed how different states within the U.S.
sentences.zh: 米歇尔还分析了美国境内的不同州

sentences.en: demonstrates strong rule following versus weak rule following.
sentences.zh: 如何表现出强烈的规则遵守与弱的规则遵守。

sentences.en: Yeah, well, I was really interested to see, you know, can we move beyond red versus blue,
sentences.zh: 是的，好吧，我真的很感兴趣，你知道，我们能否超越红色与蓝色，

sentences.en: this kind of superficial type of taxonomy to understand whether we could see differences in tightness and looseness around the country?
sentences.zh: 这种肤浅的分类法来了解我们是否能看到全国各地紧密和松散的差异？

sentences.en: And does it follow the same logic as differences at the national level?
sentences.zh: 它是否遵循与国家层面差异相同的逻辑？

sentences.en: And that's exactly what we showed.
sentences.zh: 这正是我们所展示的。

sentences.en: We can rank order the U.S.
sentences.zh: 我们可以对美国各州进行排名，

sentences.en: states and see that places in the South and in some part the Midwest, like Kansas, tend to veer tight.
sentences.zh: 看到南部和中西部部分地区，如堪萨斯州，往往偏向紧密。

sentences.en: And places on the coast, like New York and Massachusetts and California, tend to veer looser.
sentences.zh: 而沿海地区，如纽约、马萨诸塞和加利福尼亚，往往偏向松散。

sentences.en: It was really interesting because what we found was that some of the same predictors at the national level also explained tightness, looseness differences at the state level.
sentences.zh: 这真的很有趣，因为我们发现国家层面的一些相同的预测因素也解释了州层面的紧密、松散差异。

sentences.en: Tight states tended to have more natural disasters across their histories.
sentences.zh: 紧密型州在历史上往往有更多的自然灾害。

sentences.en: And they also had more pathogen prevalence and food insecurity.
sentences.zh: 它们也有更多的病原体流行和粮食不安全。

sentences.en: And loose states had more diversity in our data.
sentences.zh: 而松散型州在我们的数据中有多样性。

sentences.en: When you look at the states that you put on the spectrum, and I looked at the data, it looks like Mississippi, Alabama, Arkansas, Oklahoma, Tennessee, Texas, Louisiana, Kentucky,
sentences.zh: 当你看看你放在光谱上的州，我看了数据，看起来密西西比州、阿拉巴马州、阿肯色州、俄克拉荷马州、田纳西州、德克萨斯州、路易斯安那州、肯塔基州、

sentences.en: South Carolina, and North Carolina are the 10 tightest states.
sentences.zh: 南卡罗来纳州和北卡罗来纳州是10个最紧密的州。

sentences.en: And the loosest states in your sample were California, Oregon, Washington, Nevada, Maine, Massachusetts, Connecticut, Hawaii, New Hampshire, Vermont, and Alaska.
sentences.zh: 而你样本中最松散的州是加利福尼亚州、俄勒冈州、华盛顿州、内华达州、缅因州、马萨诸塞州、康涅狄格州、夏威夷州、新罕布什尔州、佛蒙特州和阿拉斯加州。

sentences.en: Now, every one of the top 10 tightest states is reliably Republican in presidential elections.
sentences.zh: 现在，排名前十的最严谨的州在总统选举中都是稳固的共和党阵营。

sentences.en: And nine out of the 10 looser states is reliably Democratic.
sentences.zh: 而最宽松的十个州中，有九个是稳固的民主党阵营。

sentences.en: So what's the connection between tight and loose and conservative and liberal?
sentences.zh: 那么，“严谨”与“宽松”和“保守”与“自由”之间有什么联系呢？

sentences.en: And are they actually proxies for one another?
sentences.zh: 它们实际上是彼此的代名词吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, they're really related, but they're distinct.
sentences.zh: 是的，它们确实相关，但又是不同的概念。

sentences.en: You can think about Republican-Democrat preferences at the individual level, and tightness and looseness really more at the social community level.
sentences.zh: 你可以把共和党与民主党的偏好理解为个人层面的选择，而严谨与宽松则更多是在社会群体层面。

sentences.en: But they really reinforce each other.
sentences.zh: 但它们确实会相互强化。

sentences.en: So when people really have tight mindsets, which we would suggest is more among Republicans in general, not in all domains,
sentences.zh: 所以，当人们拥有严谨的心态时——我们认为这在共和党人中更为普遍，当然并非在所有领域都是如此——

sentences.en: then they tend to create contexts that have a lot of rules.
sentences.zh: 他们往往会创造出规则繁多的环境。

sentences.en: And likewise, liberals might actually be happier in contexts where there's more permissiveness.
sentences.zh: 同样，自由派在更具包容性的环境中可能会感到更快乐。

sentences.en: So they kind of mutually reinforce each other.
sentences.zh: 所以它们在某种程度上是相互强化的。

sentences.en: But you can also envision people who are Republican or Democrat living in tight and loose environments that are mismatched with their orientation as well.
sentences.zh: 但你也可以想象，共和党人或民主党人生活在与他们自身倾向不匹配的严谨或宽松环境中。

sentences.en: To be sure, there is room for nuance in these definitions.
sentences.zh: 当然，这些定义还有细微差别的空间。

sentences.en: Some red states, for example, may prefer tight cultural attitudes, but opt for a looser approach when it comes to regulations.
sentences.zh: 例如，一些红州可能更偏好严谨的文化态度，但在监管方面却选择更宽松的方式。

sentences.en: By contrast, a culturally loose state like California can be tighter when it comes to workplace or environmental regulations.
sentences.zh: 相比之下，像加利福尼亚州这样文化上宽松的州，在工作场所或环境法规方面却可能更严谨。

sentences.en: But the tight, loose framework gives us a way of thinking about the underlying preferences that shape the way we respond to the world.
sentences.zh: 但“严谨-宽松”框架为我们提供了一种思考潜在偏好的方式，这些偏好塑造了我们应对世界的方式。

sentences.en: Coming up, understanding how nations coordinate or fail to work together when it comes to a global pandemic like the coronavirus outbreak.
sentences.zh: 接下来，我们将了解各国在面对像新冠疫情这样的全球大流行病时，是如何协调或未能协同工作的。

sentences.en: The coronavirus pandemic is changing everything really faSt.
sentences.zh: 新冠疫情正在飞速改变一切。

sentences.en: So we have created a podcast where you can hear conversations and stories from NPR journalists who are covering the pandemic, the public health fight against it,
sentences.zh: 因此，我们创建了一个播客，你可以在其中听到 NPR 记者们关于疫情、公共卫生抗疫斗争的对话和故事，

sentences.en: and how the world is coping.
sentences.zh: 以及世界是如何应对的。

sentences.en: I'm your host, Kelly McEvers.
sentences.zh: 我是主持人凯利·麦克埃弗斯（Kelly McEvers）。

sentences.en: Listen and subscribe to Coronavirus Daily from NPR.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听并订阅 NPR 的《新冠每日谈》（Coronavirus Daily）。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》（Hidden Brain）。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆（Shankar Vedantam）。

sentences.en: Michelle Galfand is a psychologist at the University of Maryland.
sentences.zh: 米歇尔·加尔凡德（Michelle Gelfand）是马里兰大学的心理学家。

sentences.en: She studies how culture shapes organizations, communities, and nations.
sentences.zh: 她研究文化如何塑造组织、社区和国家。

sentences.en: Michelle, given the large differences between nations and between communities within nations,
sentences.zh: 米歇尔，考虑到国家之间以及国家内部社区之间存在的巨大差异，

sentences.en: I want to talk about what happens when different cultural attitudes collide with one another.
sentences.zh: 我想谈谈当不同的文化态度发生碰撞时会发生什么。

sentences.en: In 1994, an American teenager was caught vandalizing some cars in Singapore.
sentences.zh: 1994年，一名美国少年在新加坡因破坏汽车被捕。

sentences.en: I want you to listen to a news clip about the story.
sentences.zh: 我想请你听一段关于这个故事的新闻片段。

sentences.en: No one knew when it would take place, but after serving five weeks of his four-month prison sentence,
sentences.zh: 没人知道它何时会发生，但在服完了四个月监禁刑期中的五周后，

sentences.en: high school student Michael Fay was flogged with a rattan cane soaked in antiseptic.
sentences.zh: 高中生迈克尔·费（Michael Fay）被处以浸泡过防腐剂的藤条鞭刑。

sentences.en: Four lashes, not six.
sentences.zh: 四鞭，不是六鞭。

sentences.en: The reduced punishment was the result of President Clinton's appeal for clemency to the Singapore government.
sentences.zh: 这种减刑是克林顿总统向新加坡政府请求宽大处理的结果。

sentences.en: Tell me what happened, Michelle.
sentences.zh: 告诉我发生了什么，米歇尔。

sentences.en: Yeah, Singapore view is really tight, and they corner the market on order.
sentences.zh: 是的，新加坡的观点非常严谨，他们垄断了秩序的市场。

sentences.en: They have very little crime.
sentences.zh: 他们的犯罪率极低。

sentences.en: They have a lot of police per capita, and in the U.S., we're much more open.
sentences.zh: 他们的人均警察数量很多，而在美国，我们开放得多。

sentences.en: We have more crime, and we have less order.
sentences.zh: 我们的犯罪率更高，秩序感更少。

sentences.en: And in this particular case, Michael Fay was caught vandalizing various property in Singapore, and he got the typical punishment, which was a fine and imprisonment,
sentences.zh: 在这个特定案例中，迈克尔·费在新加坡因破坏各种财产被捕，他受到了典型的惩罚，即罚款和监禁，

sentences.en: but also he was caned, which was a typical punishment in Singapore.
sentences.zh: 但他还被处以鞭刑，这是新加坡的一种典型惩罚。

sentences.en: And this set off really a big conflict between the U.S.
sentences.zh: 这在美国和新加坡之间引发了巨大的冲突，

sentences.en: and Singapore, including even Bill Clinton trying to get involved to get the Singapore government to be more lenient.
sentences.zh: 甚至连比尔·克林顿都试图介入，希望新加坡政府能更宽容一些。

sentences.en: And they did eventually become a little more lenient.
sentences.zh: 他们最终确实变得宽容了一些。

sentences.en: But they were also saying to us, hey, we have our own ideas about how to organize our country, and don't try to tell us how to be looser.
sentences.zh: 但他们也对我们说，嘿，我们有自己组织国家的方式，别试图教我们如何变得更宽松。

sentences.en: Look at your own New York City streets at the time and see how much disorder you have.
sentences.zh: 看看你们当时纽约市的街道，看看你们有多少混乱。

sentences.en: Leave us alone and let us manage our own country how we like.
sentences.zh: 让我们自己管理自己的国家，别管我们。

sentences.en: And this is a good example of differences in emphasis on order and openness really collide at the national level when it comes to how we organize cultural groups.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很好的例子，说明了在国家层面，对秩序和开放性的不同侧重在组织文化群体时确实会发生碰撞。

sentences.en: You have an example of cultures colliding in your own life.
sentences.zh: 你在自己的生活中也有文化碰撞的例子。

sentences.en: You're a native New Yorker, and one time you and your boyfriend were driving on Interstate 95 in South Carolina when a driver cut you off.
sentences.zh: 你是土生土长的纽约人，有一次你和男友开车在南卡罗来纳州的 95 号州际公路上行驶时，被一辆车超车切入。

sentences.en: Tell me the story of what happened next, Michelle.
sentences.zh: 告诉我们接下来发生了什么，米歇尔。

sentences.en: Yeah, this was a pretty scary situation in the early 90s.
sentences.zh: 是的，那是 90 年代初一个相当可怕的情况。

sentences.en: I was driving in South Carolina with my then boyfriend, now husband, and I come from New York where, you know, it's a pretty loose place.
sentences.zh: 当时我和我当时的男友、现在的丈夫在南卡罗来纳州开车，我来自纽约，你知道，那是一个相当宽松的地方。

sentences.en: And the South tends to be pretty tight.
sentences.zh: 而南方往往相当严谨。

sentences.en: It was founded by people who came from cultures of honor where rules are really important.
sentences.zh: 它是由来自荣誉文化的人建立的，在那里规则非常重要。

sentences.en: And so there's a lot of things that you need to be attended to in the South in terms of rules.
sentences.zh: 所以在南方，有很多事情需要注意规则。

sentences.en: And one of them is not flipping people off on the road, which was really a strong norm violation.
sentences.zh: 其中之一就是不要在路上对人竖中指，这是一种严重的违规行为。

sentences.en: And what happened to us was that we were driving along, and I guess what happened was that this car cut off our car, and so Todd just naturally just flipped him off.
sentences.zh: 发生在我们身上的事是，我们正开着车，我想是因为那辆车切入了我们的车道，所以托德（Todd）很自然地对他竖了中指。

sentences.en: And this turned into a pretty dangerous situation, a kind of road rage where we were being followed by this car.
sentences.zh: 这演变成了一个相当危险的情况，一种路怒症，我们被那辆车跟踪了。

sentences.en: We finally figured out a way to get off the road, and we sort of took a quick exit, but the car followed us off the road.
sentences.zh: 我们最终想办法下了高速，我们匆忙找了个出口，但那辆车也跟着我们下了路。

sentences.en: And I tried to get Todd to apologize to this person, and he did, and it ended well.
sentences.zh: 我试图让托德向那个人道歉，他照做了，事情最终圆满解决。

sentences.en: But it just suggests that, you know, when we're even in our own country, there's different places that have strict rules that we need to abide by,
sentences.zh: 但这只是说明，你知道，即使在我们自己的国家，也有不同的地方有着我们需要遵守的严格规则，

sentences.en: or you're going to get yourself into some serious trouble.
sentences.zh: 否则你就会陷入严重的麻烦。

sentences.en: And in other contexts, you can be much more loose.
sentences.zh: 而在其他环境下，你可以更宽松一些。

sentences.en: So the interesting thing, of course, is that in that moment, you have this what feels like a cultural altercation, and no one's actually thinking at that point.
sentences.zh: 所以有趣的是，在那一刻，你经历了一场感觉像是文化冲突的事情，而当时没有人真正去思考。

sentences.en: Well, of course, everyone flips everyone off in New York.
sentences.zh: 嗯，当然，在纽约每个人都会对别人竖中指。

sentences.en: It's what you do.
sentences.zh: 这就是你做的事。

sentences.en: It's an act of love that we can demonstrate to other people.
sentences.zh: 这是一种我们可以向他人展示的“爱的行为”。

sentences.en: I was going to say, that's right.
sentences.zh: 我正想说，没错。

sentences.en: And of course, in the South, that would be a complete no-no.
sentences.zh: 当然，在南方，那绝对是禁忌。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And in fact, when I went to Champaign-Urbana to get my PhD, I was flipping people off a lot in Champaign-Urbana.
sentences.zh: 事实上，当我去香槟-厄巴纳（Champaign-Urbana）攻读博士学位时，我在那里经常对人竖中指。

sentences.en: And I think, you know, people kind of realize, like, she's really coming from another planet.
sentences.zh: 我想，你知道，人们意识到，她真的是来自另一个星球。

sentences.en: And, you know, after five years there, I really kind of toned it down.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，在那里待了五年后，我确实收敛了很多。

sentences.en: But that's right.
sentences.zh: 但确实如此。

sentences.en: I think that that behavior is seen as really acceptable in the context of New York.
sentences.zh: 我认为这种行为在纽约的语境下被视为完全可以接受的。

sentences.en: We find some pretty interesting, also, other differences that I report on in the book, that, you know, the tight states are really very polite.
sentences.zh: 我们还发现了一些非常有趣的其他差异，我在书中也提到了，你知道，严谨的州非常礼貌。

sentences.en: Like, actually, the correlation between tightness scores and politeness scores is pretty strong.
sentences.zh: 比如，严谨得分与礼貌得分之间的相关性非常强。

sentences.en: And so loose states are seen as pretty rude, actually.
sentences.zh: 所以宽松的州实际上被视为相当粗鲁。

sentences.en: New York is ranked as the number one rudest state in the Union, my beloved New York.
sentences.zh: 纽约被评为全美最粗鲁的州，我深爱的纽约。

sentences.en: But loose states, in our research, are much more fun, according to indications of how many recreational activities there are, how many artists there are per capita.
sentences.zh: 但在我们的研究中，宽松的州更有趣，根据娱乐活动的数量、人均艺术家的数量等指标来看。

sentences.en: So you can see this kind of tightness tradeoff, this what I call the order versus openness tradeoff.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以看到这种严谨的权衡，我称之为“秩序与开放”的权衡。

sentences.en: And it's important to realize that each culture has its strength.
sentences.zh: 意识到每种文化都有其优势是很重要的。

sentences.en: And it's really important to recognize and see that they both really have strengths and liabilities.
sentences.zh: 认识到它们都有各自的优势和劣势，这一点非常重要。

sentences.en: Can you talk about the strengths of each for a moment?
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈各自的优势吗？

sentences.en: When you look at tight cultures, you mentioned a second ago that, you know, they're rule followers, they're very polite.
sentences.zh: 当你审视严谨文化时，你刚才提到，你知道，他们遵守规则，非常有礼貌。

sentences.en: But you also find correlations with things like conscientiousness and how much people help one another.
sentences.zh: 但你也发现了它们与尽责性以及人们互相帮助程度之间的相关性。

sentences.en: So talk a little bit about the strengths of tight cultures, and then we'll talk in a second about the strengths of loose cultures.
sentences.zh: 所以谈谈严谨文化的优势，然后我们再谈谈宽松文化的优势。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: I think that tight cultures corner the market on order.
sentences.zh: 我认为严谨文化垄断了秩序的市场。

sentences.en: So they have less crime.
sentences.zh: 所以他们的犯罪率更低。

sentences.en: They have more law enforcement per capita.
sentences.zh: 他们的人均执法力度更大。

sentences.en: And they're much more synchronized.
sentences.zh: 而且他们更加同步。

sentences.en: So we find that people are more likely to dress the same and drive more similar cars.
sentences.zh: 我们发现人们更有可能穿着相似，驾驶相似的汽车。

sentences.en: Even financial markets, research has shown, are more synchronized in tight cultures in terms of buying and selling stocks.
sentences.zh: 研究表明，即使是金融市场，在严谨文化中，在买卖股票方面也更加同步。

sentences.en: And another advantage of tight cultures is they have more self-control.
sentences.zh: 严谨文化的另一个优势是他们有更强的自控力。

sentences.en: So when you're in your context where there's a lot of social control, people are taught from a very early age to manage their impulses.
sentences.zh: 所以当你处于一个有大量社会控制的环境中时，人们从很小的时候就被教导要管理自己的冲动。

sentences.en: And so that means that they're more self-regulated.
sentences.zh: 这意味着他们更具自我调节能力。

sentences.en: In many different types of domains, in terms of how much they eat, we find that tight cultures have lower obesity.
sentences.zh: 在许多不同类型的领域，就饮食量而言，我们发现严谨文化的肥胖率更低。

sentences.en: They have lower debt.
sentences.zh: 他们的债务更低。

sentences.en: And they also have lower alcoholism.
sentences.zh: 而且他们的酗酒率也更低。

sentences.en: Actually, in research for the book, I found that even pets tend to be skinnier in tight cultures.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在为这本书做研究时，我发现即使是宠物在严谨文化中往往也更瘦。

sentences.en: And I can relate to that because my dog, Pepper, is pretty big.
sentences.zh: 我深有同感，因为我的狗佩珀（Pepper）体型很大。

sentences.en: And my colleague at Maryland and I always laugh, my German collaborator always laugh that he says that German dogs are much skinnier than American dogs.
sentences.zh: 我和我在马里兰州的同事总是开玩笑，我的德国合作者总是开玩笑说，德国的狗比美国的狗瘦得多。

sentences.en: But this just raises an important point that tight cultures corner the market on order and loose cultures struggle with order.
sentences.zh: 但这引出了一个重要观点：严谨文化垄断了秩序，而宽松文化在秩序方面则比较挣扎。

sentences.en: They have more crime.
sentences.zh: 他们的犯罪率更高。

sentences.en: They're less synchronized.
sentences.zh: 他们的同步性较差。

sentences.en: And they have a host of self-regulation probleMs.
sentences.zh: 而且他们有一系列自我调节方面的问题。

sentences.en: But as you mentioned, they also have their strengths.
sentences.zh: 但正如你提到的，他们也有自己的优势。

sentences.en: And so what are some of those strengths?
sentences.zh: 那么这些优势是什么呢？

sentences.en: I mean, you talked a second ago about creativity and a greater per capita number of artists.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你刚才谈到了创造力和更高的人均艺术家数量。

sentences.en: But just talk about it.
sentences.zh: 但请详细谈谈。

sentences.en: What happens in places that have these loser norms that allows them to really succeed?
sentences.zh: 在那些拥有这些宽松规范的地方，是什么让他们真正取得成功？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So I was really interested in how people react to people who were stigmatized, who look different in different cultures.
sentences.zh: 我非常感兴趣人们如何对待那些被污名化、在不同文化中看起来与众不同的人。

sentences.en: And so I did this study where I trained people from different cultures to go back to their countries.
sentences.zh: 所以我做了一项研究，我培训了来自不同文化的人，让他们回到自己的国家。

sentences.en: And I bought them fake facial warts.
sentences.zh: 我给他们买了假的脸部疣。

sentences.en: You can buy them on the Internet.
sentences.zh: 你可以在网上买到。

sentences.en: Pretty easy.
sentences.zh: 很容易。

sentences.en: And in one condition, they were wearing fake facial warts on their faces.
sentences.zh: 在一种情况下，他们脸上戴着假的脸部疣。

sentences.en: And then in another condition, they were wearing tattoos and nose rings and purple hair.
sentences.zh: 在另一种情况下，他们戴着纹身、鼻环和紫色的头发。

sentences.en: And then in another condition, they were just wearing their plain face.
sentences.zh: 在另一种情况下，他们只是保持原本的面貌。

sentences.en: And I had a simple experiment where we had them go around the world and ask for help on city streets or ask for help in stores.
sentences.zh: 我做了一个简单的实验，让他们在世界各地走动，在城市街道或商店里寻求帮助。

sentences.en: And what was interesting is that when people were wearing their normal face,
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，当人们保持原本面貌时，

sentences.en: there was no difference in whether people were likely to help them around the world in terms of giving them directions or giving them help in stores.
sentences.zh: 无论是在指路还是在商店提供帮助方面，世界各地的人们是否愿意帮助他们并没有什么区别。

sentences.en: But when they were wearing these weird facial warts or tattoos, we found that people in loose cultures were much more likely to help them as compared to tight cultures.
sentences.zh: 但当他们戴着这些奇怪的脸部疣或纹身时，我们发现，与严谨文化相比，宽松文化中的人们更有可能帮助他们。

sentences.en: So we can see that there's a big difference in how people react to the stigmatized around the world.
sentences.zh: 所以我们可以看到，世界各地人们对被污名化者的反应存在巨大差异。

sentences.en: And this is not just in city streets.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是在城市街道上。

sentences.en: It's on surveys.
sentences.zh: 在调查中也是如此。

sentences.en: It's with implicit attitudes.
sentences.zh: 在内隐态度中也是如此。

sentences.en: So loose cultures corner the market on openness.
sentences.zh: 所以宽松文化垄断了开放性的市场。

sentences.en: And so if you look at something like xenophobia, for example, you're likely to see far less xenophobia in a loose culture than in a tight culture.
sentences.zh: 如果你看看像仇外心理这样的问题，你会发现宽松文化中的仇外心理远少于严谨文化。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So people are much more open to people of different races, religions, of immigrants, people with disabilities and many different other stigmas.
sentences.zh: 所以人们对不同种族、宗教、移民、残疾人以及许多其他带有污名的人更加开放。

sentences.en: And tight cultures struggle with openness.
sentences.zh: 而严谨文化在开放性方面则比较挣扎。

sentences.en: When you look at the tension between these different attitudes, Michelle, the looseness, tightness tension, how does this play out within organizations, which obviously, you know,
sentences.zh: 米歇尔，当你审视这些不同态度之间的张力时，这种宽松与严谨的张力，在组织内部是如何体现的？显然，你知道，

sentences.en: hire people from both tight and loose cultures?
sentences.zh: 他们雇佣来自严谨和宽松两种文化的人。

sentences.en: Yeah, actually, you could see that the same principle that culture is invisible in organizations applies even when companies are merging.
sentences.zh: 是的，实际上，你可以看到文化在组织中是隐形的，这一原则即使在公司合并时也适用。

sentences.en: Often it's the case they choose each other based on strategic advantages,
sentences.zh: 通常情况下，他们基于战略优势选择彼此，

sentences.en: but they don't tend to see the deep cultural iceberg of tightness and looseness that's really beneath the surface.
sentences.zh: 但他们往往看不到隐藏在表面之下的严谨与宽松的深层文化冰山。

sentences.en: So think back to a great example of tight, loose conflict happened in a Daimler-Chrysler merger, where these two companies coming from the U.S., Chrysler and Daimler, from Germany,
sentences.zh: 回想一下戴姆勒-克莱斯勒（Daimler-Chrysler）合并中发生的严谨与宽松冲突的绝佳例子，这两家公司分别来自美国（克莱斯勒）和德国（戴姆勒），

sentences.en: at first glance, it seemed like a match made in heaven.
sentences.zh: 乍一看，这似乎是天作之合。

sentences.en: And a lot of people thought this was going to be a great marriage.
sentences.zh: 很多人认为这将是一场伟大的联姻。

sentences.en: But in fact, their cultural differences in tightness and looseness seem to really rear their ugly head, such that sometime after they're merged,
sentences.zh: 但事实上，他们在严谨和宽松方面的文化差异似乎真的暴露了丑陋的一面，以至于在合并一段时间后，

sentences.en: we see that they actually experienced a larger cultural conflict and they divorced, as people would say.
sentences.zh: 我们看到他们实际上经历了更大的文化冲突，正如人们所说，他们“离婚”了。

sentences.en: And it makes sense.
sentences.zh: 这很有道理。

sentences.en: The people, the practices and the leadership is profoundly different in tight and loose organizations.
sentences.zh: 严谨和宽松组织中的人员、实践和领导力有着深刻的不同。

sentences.en: And when they come to collide, we see that it actually could be very costly.
sentences.zh: 当它们发生碰撞时，我们看到这实际上可能代价高昂。

sentences.en: In a recent study, we actually studied thousands of cross-border acquisitions, and we could see that differences in tightness and looseness between them was costly,
sentences.zh: 在最近的一项研究中，我们实际上研究了数千起跨境收购，我们可以看到它们之间在严谨和宽松方面的差异代价高昂，

sentences.en: even as much as $250 million when you see big differences in tight, loose.
sentences.zh: 当你看到严谨与宽松的巨大差异时，损失甚至高达 2.5 亿美元。

sentences.en: And I imagine the same thing also happens within organizations that are not merging with other organizations.
sentences.zh: 我想，在那些没有进行合并的组织内部，同样的事情也会发生。

sentences.en: You know, you're hiring someone from New York, and you're hiring someone from Kansas.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你雇佣了一个来自纽约的人，又雇佣了一个来自堪萨斯州的人。

sentences.en: They're working next to one another, and they have potentially different attitudes.
sentences.zh: 他们并肩工作，但可能有着不同的态度。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: And in fact, a lot of organizations, within organizations, there's lots of differences in tightness and looseness.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在许多组织内部，在“紧”和“松”的程度上存在着很大的差异。

sentences.en: Think about sales versus an R&D versus accounting.
sentences.zh: 想想销售部门、研发部门和会计部门之间的区别吧。

sentences.en: It makes sense that these groups would veer differently on tightness and looseness.
sentences.zh: 这些群体在“紧”和“松”的倾向上有所不同，这是合情合理的。

sentences.en: And in fact, the people who are attracted to those kinds of jobs likely have tight and loose mindsets that really cause a lot of conflict when they interact with each other.
sentences.zh: 事实上，那些被这类工作吸引的人，很可能拥有“紧”或“松”的思维模式，当他们互动时，确实会引发很多冲突。

sentences.en: Sometimes organizations who want to loosen up, for example, I interviewed people in manufacturing firms who said, hey, we want to become more innovative.
sentences.zh: 有时，那些想要变得“松”一点的组织，比如我采访过的一些制造企业，他们说，嘿，我们想变得更具创新性。

sentences.en: We're going to hire groups to help us do that that are much looser.
sentences.zh: 我们要雇佣一些更“松”的团队来帮助我们实现这一目标。

sentences.en: But what we found was that they actually had so much cultural conflict.
sentences.zh: 但我们发现，他们实际上产生了太多的文化冲突。

sentences.en: When you're used to a lot of order and efficiency, and then you hire a group that's much more creative and may miss some deadlines, this causes a lot of cultural conflict.
sentences.zh: 当你习惯了高度的秩序和效率，然后雇佣了一个更具创造力、可能会错过一些截止日期的团队时，这就会引发大量的文化冲突。

sentences.en: And so I think if we can think about tightness and looseness as it relates to mergers, we can anticipate these conflicts better and negotiate them ahead of time.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，如果我们能从合并的角度来思考“紧”和“松”，我们就能更好地预见这些冲突，并提前进行协商。

sentences.en: How do you prevent this work from becoming a form of essentialism, if you will, where you basically say, all right,
sentences.zh: 你如何防止这项工作变成一种本质主义，即你基本上说，好吧，

sentences.en: now I'm seeing that there's a risk when you have a German company merging with an American company.
sentences.zh: 我现在看到，当一家德国公司与一家美国公司合并时，存在风险。

sentences.en: And so I'm oversimplifying these findings and say, okay, all American companies should never look to German companies to form a merger,
sentences.zh: 于是我过度简化了这些发现，说，好吧，所有美国公司都不应该考虑与德国公司合并，

sentences.en: or you should never put a New Yorker in the same room as someone from Kansas.
sentences.zh: 或者你不应该把一个纽约人和一个堪萨斯州人放在同一个房间里。

sentences.en: And then you have, you know, some of the problems that you have with personality tests,
sentences.zh: 然后你就会遇到一些性格测试中存在的问题，

sentences.en: where you have basically these general tendencies amplified to a point where people are taking them perhaps a little too seriously.
sentences.zh: 基本上就是这些普遍倾向被放大到了人们可能看得太认真的地步。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think this is a really important point, because, you know, this construct,
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为这是一个非常重要的观点，因为，你知道，这个概念，

sentences.en: we can apply it across different levels and certain occupations and certain industries in the US veer tighter, the military, airlines, nuclear power plants, hospitals,
sentences.zh: 我们可以将其应用于不同的层面，在美国，某些职业和某些行业倾向于更“紧”，比如军队、航空公司、核电站、医院，

sentences.en: they need stronger rules.
sentences.zh: 他们需要更严格的规则。

sentences.en: Other occupations and industries are much looser.
sentences.zh: 而其他职业和行业则要“松”得多。

sentences.en: So even in the US, we don't have one organizational culture, clearly.
sentences.zh: 所以即使在美国，显然也没有统一的组织文化。

sentences.en: And again, at the individual level, we all lean tighter loose for good reasons, but there's certain domains that we might be tighter or looser in.
sentences.zh: 同样，在个人层面上，我们每个人都有理由偏向“紧”或“松”，但在某些领域，我们可能会表现得更“紧”或更“松”。

sentences.en: So the more important point is to diagnose the levels of tight and loose in context where we're merging and figure out where our strengths are and where our liabilities are and talk about them,
sentences.zh: 所以更重要的一点是，在我们要合并的环境中诊断“紧”和“松”的程度，找出我们的优势和劣势，并讨论它们，

sentences.en: have cultural conversations, have conversations about culture, negotiate culture ahead of time.
sentences.zh: 进行文化对话，讨论文化，提前协商文化。

sentences.en: But the important thing is to really understand that culture is driving a lot of the conflict in the first place.
sentences.zh: 但最重要的是要真正理解，文化本身就是导致冲突的主要原因。

sentences.en: So when you look at the US as a whole, you also find that the degree of tightness within the US has changed over time.
sentences.zh: 所以当你审视整个美国时，你也会发现美国内部的“紧”度随着时间的推移发生了变化。

sentences.en: Talk about that.
sentences.zh: 谈谈这个。

sentences.en: How has it changed?
sentences.zh: 它是如何变化的？

sentences.en: In what direction?
sentences.zh: 朝着什么方向？

sentences.en: And what are the drivers?
sentences.zh: 驱动因素是什么？

sentences.en: Yeah, it's a great question.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一个很好的问题。

sentences.en: What we found was striking is that over the last 200 years, we've become much looser.
sentences.zh: 我们发现令人震惊的是，在过去的200年里，我们变得“松”多了。

sentences.en: And what we can see is that it's associated with this exact order and openness tradeoff I was mentioning.
sentences.zh: 我们可以看到，这与我提到的那种秩序与开放的权衡有关。

sentences.en: So looseness has really caused much more creativity, patents, and so forth, but it's also produced less order, more debt, for example.
sentences.zh: 所以“松”确实带来了更多的创造力、专利等等，但也导致了秩序的减少，比如更多的债务。

sentences.en: And so we can see that the US has changed, it's become more loose, and it has the same associated tradeoffs.
sentences.zh: 所以我们可以看到美国已经发生了变化，它变得更“松”了，并且有着同样的权衡。

sentences.en: Of course, we can also see that during times of threat, we tend to tighten up.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们也可以看到，在受到威胁时，我们往往会变得更“紧”。

sentences.en: And so we can also see this as a dynamic construct, that it's not as though the world's becoming looser.
sentences.zh: 所以我们也可以将其视为一个动态的概念，并不是说世界正在变得越来越“松”。

sentences.en: When we have collective threats, we can also see shifts to tightness.
sentences.zh: 当我们面临集体威胁时，我们也能看到向“紧”的转变。

sentences.en: So when you're speaking about collective threats, it makes me think, of course, of the coronavirus outbreak that we are experiencing right now in 2020.
sentences.zh: 所以当你谈到集体威胁时，我自然会想到我们现在2020年正在经历的冠状病毒疫情。

sentences.en: And when you look at how different countries in the world are coping with the coronavirus outbreak, do you see the same hand of culture at play?
sentences.zh: 当你观察世界各国如何应对冠状病毒疫情时，你是否看到了同样的文化之手在起作用？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that it's really important to think about the spread of corona, not just from a medical point of view, but also from a cultural point of view.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为不仅要从医学角度，还要从文化角度来思考冠状病毒的传播，这一点非常重要。

sentences.en: And we see striking differences around the world in response to corona.
sentences.zh: 我们看到世界各地在应对冠状病毒方面存在显著差异。

sentences.en: You know, tight societies like Singapore and Hong Kong, for example, have demonstrated a really effective, quick, swift response.
sentences.zh: 你知道，像新加坡和香港这样的“紧”社会，已经展示了非常有效、迅速的反应。

sentences.en: Singapore has had very few deaths.
sentences.zh: 新加坡的死亡人数非常少。

sentences.en: And the United States, the response so far echoes our loose cultural programming.
sentences.zh: 而美国，目前的反应呼应了我们“松”的文化程序。

sentences.en: It's been conflicted.
sentences.zh: 它是冲突的。

sentences.en: It's been unstandardized.
sentences.zh: 它是非标准化的。

sentences.en: It's been uncoordinated.
sentences.zh: 它是缺乏协调的。

sentences.en: And I think that, you know,
sentences.zh: 我认为，你知道，

sentences.en: this is a cultural issue because loose cultures who have had gender to have less threat haven't had the kind of context where they realize the importance of sacrificing liberty and autonomy and freedom for constraint and rules.
sentences.zh: 这是一个文化问题，因为那些习惯了较少威胁的“松”文化，并没有意识到为了约束和规则而牺牲自由和自主权的重要性。

sentences.en: And we have kind of an ambivalence about tightness in the United States and in general.
sentences.zh: 在美国，我们对“紧”有一种矛盾心理。

sentences.en: And here's where we see that this is a real liability, that we do see in our data analyses that loose cultures have had higher spread of the disease,
sentences.zh: 在这里我们看到这是一个真正的劣势，我们在数据分析中确实看到，“松”文化导致了疾病的更高传播，

sentences.en: different trajectories than tighter cultures.
sentences.zh: 与“紧”文化有着不同的轨迹。

sentences.en: And that's not to say that we should give up our creative loose spirit.
sentences.zh: 这并不是说我们应该放弃我们创造性的“松”精神。

sentences.en: It just means that we need to tighten up to fight the disease.
sentences.zh: 这只是意味着我们需要“紧”起来以对抗疾病。

sentences.en: And we need to use our loose spirit to create technologies that can help us to fight it as well.
sentences.zh: 我们需要利用我们的“松”精神来创造能够帮助我们对抗疾病的技术。

sentences.en: So if you look at countries like Spain and Italy, for example, presumably these are loser cultures.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你看看西班牙和意大利这样的国家，据推测这些是更“松”的文化。

sentences.en: They seem to have very different trajectories of the coronavirus outbreak than countries like South Korea.
sentences.zh: 它们似乎与韩国等国家有着截然不同的冠状病毒疫情轨迹。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's right.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: I think that Italy in our research was also veered loose and Spain as well.
sentences.zh: 我认为在我们的研究中，意大利和西班牙也偏向“松”。

sentences.en: And you could see that, and of course it's multiply determined, it's not just determined by tightness, looseness, but it is,
sentences.zh: 你可以看到这一点，当然这是多重因素决定的，不仅仅是由“紧”或“松”决定的，但确实，

sentences.en: you could see that the response in Italy is something that we see here in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 你可以看到意大利的反应与我们在美国看到的类似，

sentences.en: as well.
sentences.zh: 也是如此。

sentences.en: That even people had harder time obeying the rules, even under the quarantines early on, people were trying to leave their communities, which was also causing further spread.
sentences.zh: 即使在早期隔离期间，人们也很难遵守规则，人们试图离开他们的社区，这也导致了进一步的传播。

sentences.en: And I think that if we think about the meaning of rules, it would help us to tighten up more quickly.
sentences.zh: 我认为如果我们思考规则的意义，将有助于我们更快地“紧”起来。

sentences.en: So I think if we think about rules are important to keep us safe, that maybe we'd be more amenable to social distancing and hand washing.
sentences.zh: 所以如果我们认为规则对于保护我们的安全很重要，也许我们会更乐于接受社交距离和勤洗手。

sentences.en: But we really do need to change our cultural programming in this context.
sentences.zh: 但我们确实需要在这个背景下改变我们的文化程序。

sentences.en: The problem is that it's hard for us to give up liberty for constraint, but it's critical for our safety.
sentences.zh: 问题在于，我们很难为了约束而放弃自由，但这对于我们的安全至关重要。

sentences.en: So the interesting thing, of course, is that because most of us don't think about these underlying systems that drive whether we are rule followers or rule breakers,
sentences.zh: 所以有趣的是，因为我们大多数人不会去思考那些决定我们是规则追随者还是规则破坏者的潜在系统，

sentences.en: we just assume that the way we are is the way the world ought to be,
sentences.zh: 我们只是认为我们现在的样子就是世界本该有的样子，

sentences.en: it becomes quite difficult when you have a situation that suddenly calls for you to exercise a completely different system, right?
sentences.zh: 当你突然面临一种需要你运用完全不同系统的情况时，这就会变得非常困难，对吧？

sentences.en: So if you are part of a tight culture and you're hearing an authoritarian government tell you, you know, everyone stays put and everyone follows the rules,
sentences.zh: 所以如果你身处一个“紧”文化中，听到威权政府告诉你，每个人都待在原地，每个人都遵守规则，

sentences.en: really easy for you to do.
sentences.zh: 这对你来说很容易做到。

sentences.en: But if you come from a loose culture and you suddenly have a government play the heavy and basically say everyone stays home, business is shut down,
sentences.zh: 但如果你来自一个“松”文化，而政府突然采取强硬手段，基本上说每个人都待在家里，企业关闭，

sentences.en: there's a part of you that sort of says, hang on, why should I do that?
sentences.zh: 你内心会有一种声音说，等等，我为什么要那样做？

sentences.en: And I think the point that I'm trying to make is that it's one thing to say that we should judiciously decide when to be tight and when to be loose.
sentences.zh: 我想表达的观点是，说我们应该明智地决定何时“紧”、何时“松”是一回事。

sentences.en: But I think the paradox here is that because we're not even aware of being tight or loose, we just assume the way we are is the way we ought to be.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这里的悖论在于，因为我们甚至没有意识到自己是“紧”还是“松”，我们只是认为我们现在的样子就是我们本该有的样子。

sentences.en: It's very difficult to change on a dime when the situation around us changes.
sentences.zh: 当周围的情况发生变化时，很难立即做出改变。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that's precisely right.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为这非常正确。

sentences.en: And I think these are cultural matters of life and death in my point of view.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，这些都是关乎生死的文化问题。

sentences.en: I think that if we think about this as a temporary shift, that in context of threat, we know from research that we need strong rules to coordinate to survive.
sentences.zh: 我认为如果我们认为这只是一个暂时的转变，在威胁的背景下，我们从研究中知道，我们需要强有力的规则来协调以求生存。

sentences.en: You can see this approach in China.
sentences.zh: 你可以看到中国采取了这种方法。

sentences.en: They tightened up very quickly in a massive way.
sentences.zh: 他们非常迅速地以大规模的方式“紧”了起来。

sentences.en: They had clearly huge quarantines.
sentences.zh: 他们显然进行了大规模的隔离。

sentences.en: They were citizens were on watch for people that might be showing symptoMs.
sentences.zh: 公民们都在留意可能出现症状的人。

sentences.en: They had temperature thermometers checking people's temperature, people knocking on people's door to check this.
sentences.zh: 他们有温度计来检查人们的体温，有人敲门来检查这一点。

sentences.en: It's all in the spirit of trying to control the disease.
sentences.zh: 这一切都是为了控制疾病。

sentences.en: As it's gotten controlled, there's obviously much less restriction now in Wuhan and other areas.
sentences.zh: 随着疫情得到控制，武汉和其他地区的限制显然少多了。

sentences.en: So we can think about this as temporarily tightening up to flatten the curve.
sentences.zh: 所以我们可以认为这是为了拉平曲线而暂时“紧”起来。

sentences.en: And I think that we need strong leadership to tell us that this is the appropriate response in this situation.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们需要强有力的领导来告诉我们，这是在这种情况下适当的反应。

sentences.en: And research suggests that that's the case.
sentences.zh: 研究表明确实如此。

sentences.en: So I understand that people always ask you, which is better, tight or loose?
sentences.zh: 所以我明白人们总是问你，是“紧”好还是“松”好？

sentences.en: What do you tell them, Misha?
sentences.zh: 你告诉他们什么，Misha？

sentences.en: You know, this is something that we've been thinking about.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是我们一直在思考的问题。

sentences.en: Philosophers have been talking about for centuries.
sentences.zh: 哲学家们几个世纪以来一直在讨论这个问题。

sentences.en: You know, have people like Plato and Confucius and Hobbes say, no, we need tightness.
sentences.zh: 你知道，像柏拉图、孔子和霍布斯这样的人说，不，我们需要“紧”。

sentences.en: We need constraint.
sentences.zh: 我们需要约束。

sentences.en: Hobbes in particular had a pretty negative view of human nature.
sentences.zh: 霍布斯尤其对人性持相当负面的看法。

sentences.en: And then you have people like John Stuart Mill and Freud.
sentences.zh: 然后你有像约翰·斯图尔特·密尔和弗洛伊德这样的人。

sentences.en: Freud in particular thought rules make you neurotic.
sentences.zh: 弗洛伊德特别认为规则会让你神经质。

sentences.en: And so what's the answer?
sentences.zh: 那么答案是什么？

sentences.en: Is it tight or loose?
sentences.zh: 是“紧”还是“松”？

sentences.en: I had the hunch that maybe it's neither.
sentences.zh: 我有一种预感，也许两者都不是。

sentences.en: Groups clearly need to veer tight or loose for good reasons based on their degree of threat.
sentences.zh: 群体显然需要根据威胁程度有理由地偏向“紧”或“松”。

sentences.en: But what I found is that the groups that get too extreme in either direction really are dysfunctional.
sentences.zh: 但我发现，在任何一个方向上走得太极端的群体确实是功能失调的。

sentences.en: So extreme tightness or extreme looseness produces higher suicide and less happiness.
sentences.zh: 所以极端的“紧”或极端的“松”会导致更高的自杀率和更少的幸福感。

sentences.en: And this is what I call the Goldilocks principle of tight, loose, that we need some kind of cultural balance.
sentences.zh: 这就是我所说的“紧”“松”的“金发姑娘原则”，我们需要某种文化平衡。

sentences.en: Really, I think we need to be ambidextrous, like using the right and the left hand when it comes to tight, loose.
sentences.zh: 真的，我认为我们需要左右开弓，就像在处理“紧”和“松”时同时使用左右手一样。

sentences.en: And we need leadership to help us deploy tightness under the right circumstances and looseness under others.
sentences.zh: 我们需要领导力来帮助我们在适当的情况下部署“紧”，在其他情况下部署“松”。
